best_for: Java and PHP developers, students and teachers who want a free IDE with refactoring and project wizards in the box, and no paid edition to outgrow.
description:
Apache NetBeans is a development environment that began at Sun Microsystems, moved to Oracle, and was given to the Apache Software Foundation in 2016. It became a top-level Apache project in April 2019, and many developers know it as the original free Java IDE.

Inspect and Transform, in the Refactor menu, scans a file, a package or a whole project for code patterns and shows the suggested changes in a preview before you apply them. You can also write your own inspection scripts. More features come from the plugin portal at plugins.netbeans.apache.org. If you build desktop apps in Java, the NetBeans Platform gives you window management, saved state and menu and shortcut wiring for Swing programs, so you do not write that plumbing yourself.

points.title: Java first, web languages too
points.text: The project lists editors, wizards and templates for Java, PHP, JavaScript, HTML5 and CSS. The editor highlights code by meaning as well as syntax and has several refactoring tools, so renaming or moving code across a project is one action.

points.title: Free under Apache 2.0
points.text: NetBeans is an Apache Software Foundation project released under the Apache License 2.0, so it costs nothing to use, change or share.

points.title: Bring a JDK 21 or newer
points.text: NetBeans 32 runs on JDK 21, 25 or 27, and the project suggests the latest update release. The JDK that runs the IDE does not limit which JDK your projects build against.

points.title: Installers come from committers, not Apache
points.text: Apache itself releases only a platform-independent zip and the source. Packaged installers and the Snap are made by NetBeans committers as a convenience and are not ASF releases. Some of them bundle a JDK under extra license terms.

points.title: Four releases a year
points.text: A new numbered release ships about every three months. NetBeans 32 came out on November 16, 2026. Older releases stay downloadable from Apache's archive, but they no longer get support or fixes.

points.title: Windows lags behind here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 8 versions, and its newest is 25. macOS lists only 31 and Linux only 32, so downgrades there need another source. For the current release on Windows, use the zip from Apache. Windows on Arm is not a fully supported platform.

points.title: The Flatpak is not marked verified
points.text: The Linux build here is a Flathub package for x64 and Arm64 under the Apache Software Foundation name, but Flathub does not mark it as verified. It is a large download, about 1 GB.
